Lagging is the safe direction (the marker points where you have been, never where you have not earned), and the session latch stops it walking backwards while you play, so I kept them. WHY MEDIUM: the ladder itself is only three rungs and I am confident in all three, but the mission is a stopwatch and the addon cannot see a clock. You have 24 game hours (one Earth hour) on the first run, 48 on a repeat, you must kill THIRTY monsters, and you must report in the FINAL game hour -- earlier only tells you how long is left, later fails the mission outright. None of kills, game time or the deadline is in any packet, so the middle rung can never be observed to be done and the last one can never be known to be safe.

THE REPEAT IS A DIFFERENT ZONE. First time it is Tahrongi Canyon; repeating it is Buburimu Peninsula with double the time. Only one of the two can be the ladder, so the spine is the first-time run and the repeat is on the step's note. Both 'After the walkthrough' sections are steps; 'Getting Assessed' is the reporting rule and the failure clause, so its bullet [2] (what happens if you fail) is not a step.

THE BRANCH IS THE WHOLE PAGE. Four 'After the walkthrough' sections are two complete alternative routes: Windurst-to-Bastok then Bastok-to-San d'Oria, or Windurst-to-San d'Oria then San d'Oria-to-Bastok. Both nations are visited either way, but WHAT you do in each depends on which you did first -- go to Bastok first and the Bastok leg is Pius, Grohm's three Pickaxes, Mine Gravel from the Mythril Seams in Palborough Mines and Mythril Sand from the refiner, and San d'Oria then ends in the Horlais Peak BCNM 'The Rank 2 Final Mission' against the Dread Dragon; go to San d'Oria first and that leg ends by killing Warchief Vatgit in Ghelsba Outpost, and Bastok then ends in the Waughroon Shrine BCNM against the Dark Dragon. No single ordered ladder is true for both players, so I modelled the SPINE only: Kupipi, the two consulates as an unordered pair (which is exactly what the page's own bullet 1 says -- pick whichever nation you like first), and Kupipi again. The two legs' interiors are in the notes and are deliberately not rungs; a merged path would send somebody to a BCNM they are not doing.

EVIDENCE: only the Letter to the consuls, given by Kupipi and carried through both legs. It resolves to three key item ids (5,6,7), one per nation of origin, and resolve.lua says any of them satisfies it. The Adventurer's Certificate, the 3,000 gil and the Rank 3 promotion are all header rewards and so are not evidence. Cipher: Semih and Cipher: Halver are Trust rewards, not steps.

Heavens Tower is its own zone off Windurst Walls in the client (zone 242), so Kupipi's rungs are zoned there and not to Windurst Walls. Patt-Pott is in 'Metalworks' -- the wiki's 'Bastok Metalworks' does not resolve.

EVIDENCE IS EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and that is the interesting decision here. The one key item the walkthrough hands out, the Starway Stairway bauble, is ALSO listed in the header's Reward line, and hard rule 7 says a reward proves the mission is over rather than that a step is done. So the bauble is not used, and this five-rung ladder carries no evidence at all -- which the brief says is normal and correct for missions. It is worth saying plainly, because the bauble is granted at step 1 and is permanent (it is what unlocks the upper tower), so it would otherwise have been the sturdiest evidence in the batch; the rule forbids it and I did not reach around the rule.

STEP 4: the page says to FALL down the trap door -- the cutscene is in the pit, so the failure mode is opening the door instead. Two switches flank an obvious floor panel and which one drops you changes daily, and the sub-bullet is explicit that the person on the mission must pull it themselves. The page calls them 'switches' in one line and 'the lever' in the next; 'Lever' is the name that resolves, and it is zoned to Castle Oztroja so validate.py's ambiguous-name-without-zone gate does not bite. The Blank Target in that room belongs to the Onion Rings quest and is not a step here.

CORRECTION under the rewritten hard rule 7: the 'EVIDENCE IS EMPTY ON PURPOSE' paragraph above is superseded -- walkthrough bullet 1 of 5 explicitly hands over the Starway Stairway bauble rather than the header's Reward line being its only mention, so it is now recorded as step 1's evidence (name resolves, ki id 36), and the older review flag reward_blocks_evidence is left in place only because this narrow pass does not remove flags; it should be dropped. || LEAD: the flag(s) ['reward_blocks_evidence'] were removed -- they asserted the reward key item was NOT used as evidence, which the rule-7 rewrite reversed. THE TWO KEY ROUTES CONVERGE, so they are ONE rung. 'Obtaining Delkfutt Key Short Way' and 'Obtaining Delkfutt Key Long Way' (with 'Navigation') differ only in how you reach Porphyrion -- the short way opens the door at (J-8), rides the ??? at the foot of the stairs in Upper Delkfutt's Tower and lands next to him; the long way is a twelve-floor climb past Mimas. Both end with the same NM and the same key item, and bullet 4 says a player who already holds either the item Delkfutt Key or the key item skips the whole thing. Modelling that as two ladders would send half the players up a tower they do not need; modelling it as one rung anchored on Porphyrion marks the thing they both have to reach.

The three magicites themselves are an unordered set -- the page asks for all three and names no order -- so they share the group 'magicite' and draw at once. Their PREREQUISITES are ordered inside themselves (an NM must die before its drop can be traded, Paya-Sabya before Muckvix), so they are not grouped; the note says they are independent of one another.

WHY MEDIUM -- THE PAGE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT THE KEY. The 'Castle Oztroja' section says the Brass Door on the top floor (Map 4, H-5) is the one that needs the key that drops from Yagudo Flagellants; the 'Maps' section says the large Brass Door up there is opened by lighting the unlit Torch in a corner room, and that the Judgment Key is traded to a SMALLER Brass Door on the platform after you fall through the Brass Statue's trapdoor. Both are on the page. I followed the Maps section, which is the one giving step-by-step instructions, put the Judgment Key trade on the door after the fall, and recorded the (H-5) door and the torch in the notes -- but a player who reads the other section will be looking at a different door, so this is flagged rather than smoothed over.

EVIDENCE: four rungs carry it -- the Holy One's invitation from the door, the Balga champion certificate from the BCNM, the Judgment Key (an ITEM, not a key item) off the Flagellants, and the Holy One's oath from Kaa Toru the Just. The Ashura Necklace arrives with the oath but is in the header's Reward line, so rule 7 bars it; the oath is not in that line and is obtained at its own step, so it stands.
